A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAD research, with matching authors, method, and experimental framework. All 27 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison; relocated text, figures, and tables can be matched.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original hazardous-generation, jailbreak, memorization, sensitivity, and throughput results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments, revises several jailbreak results, and adds utility measurements to the baseline comparison.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same unsafe-reference denoiser approximation, guidance strength, active timestep window, and prompt conditioning. Notation and explanatory edits do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RTP hazardous and benign prompting, RTP/ToxiGen/BeaverTails reference datasets, five jailbreak benchmarks, and WikiText-103 memorization tasks. Random and contiguous masking evaluations already appear in v1; completed StrongREJECT entries do not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 8 retains Best-of-N with N=8 and FK Steering with k=4 and k=8. Jailbreak comparisons retain the undefended model, PPL filtering, self-reminder, and DiffuGuard, with and without SAD. Filled result cells do not establish added comparators.

E3.justification: Table 8 extends the reported baseline evaluation to BERTScore on benign RTP controls, alongside unsafe rate, perplexity, and time. Existing sampling settings and budgets remain stated as before. The large DIJA result replacements do not establish a changed attack procedure or experimental rerun.

E4.justification: The revised DIJA robustness evidence substantially changes the observed failure profile, especially on AdvBench: apparent widespread refusal becomes frequent successful attacks with generally limited SAD protection. StrongREJECT robustness evidence is also completed. The guidance-strength, timestep, reference-size, and memorization ablations and the qualitative examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: V2 removes Table 2's historical reference to a prior single-seed DIJA submission and restricts the small-sample variance explanation in Appendix C.4 to JailbreakBench. Fixed-seed reporting and the 10,000-trial memorization estimation remain unchanged; no additional repetitions, intervals, or significance tests are established.

E6.justification: Table 13 replaces LLaDA-Instruct's DIJA/no-defence Base/SAD ASR of 0.0/0.0 with 83.1/82.7, and Dream-Instruct's 31.3/12.1 with 84.6/81.0. Tables 10 and 14 also replace substantial DIJA results; Tables 17–18 fill or revise StrongREJECT entries. Table 8 adds BERTScores, and Table 2 corrects a refusal-delta sign. These are revised reported outcomes, not demonstrated changes in method performance.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1, the categorical-kernel derivation, denoiser approximations, metric definitions, and discoverable-extraction formulation are retained. Changes from q to qt and equation placement are not substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims of training-free safety guidance, formal safety guarantees, reduced hazardous generation and memorization, jailbreak robustness, and preserved generation quality.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly attributes FK Steering's higher BERTScore to its lack of intervention on benign prompts and interprets SAD's 0.018 decrease as negligible. Appendix C.4 narrows the small-benchmark explanation to JailbreakBench. Section 5.2 also newly mislabels percentage-point reductions of 16.6 and 10.2 as relative percentages.

D1.justification: The reported code repository changes from ammanyusuf/SAD to ParkLabML/SAD. Appendix C.2 additionally describes FK Steering's behavior on benign prompts. Hardware, training details, and principal sampling hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes principally update publication metadata, identify the formerly anonymous SGF citation as Kim et al. (2026), and update the title and venue of the existing Kirchhof work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose and paragraph edits, updates the publication block and bibliography, and renames Broader Impact to Impact Statement. The overall section order and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Plots receive styling and legend changes while retaining their plotted evidence. Figure 3's caption is corrected to describe metric values rather than changes. Table 8 gains a BERTScore column and note, and several figures, tables, and qualitative examples shift with page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a more complete and internally consistent empirical record: Table 10's DIJA refusal rates now agree with Table 2, missing StrongREJECT results are supplied, and Table 8 exposes an additional utility tradeoff. These reporting gains are limited by unexplained large DIJA replacements and new interpretation errors: Section 5.1 claims better BERTScore despite SAD scoring 0.537 versus FK Steering's 0.573, Table 8 incorrectly labels all metrics lower-is-better, and Section 5.2 confuses percentage-point and relative reductions.
